- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.2) — add 3–7% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
- Lagged price movements often overshoot — adjust 3–5 days ahead by subtracting 1–3% from forecast to correct for momentum decay.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), reduce forecast slope for next 5–7 days to avoid overcorrection.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.7 to -0.3) triggers downward correction — reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 3–5 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in cycle — cap forecast at 10% above 14-day moving average to avoid overextension.
